title: The Soul Train
theme: For over three decades, one show was the essential stage for Black music in America. Soul Train. Don Cornelius built it. A generation of artists defined themselves on it. This episode is about the performances, the artists, and the institution itself.
narrativePurpose: Test knowledge of Soul Train's landmark performances, the artists who defined the show, the music behind those moments, and the history of the program that changed American television.
toneProgression: The iconic performances and artists everyone knows → the music, songwriting, and production behind them → the archival history of Soul Train itself and the connections that shaped the era

vault.note: Digit 4 (index 3) is always visible. Vault code 1-9-7-4 — the year Soul Train hosted landmark performances from Rufus, James Brown, Labelle, and Marvin Gaye in a single season, cementing its place as the essential stage for Black music and culture. 1974: the year Soul Train's golden era peaked.

rounds.name: RADIO HITS
rounds.description: The artists and performances that defined Soul Train — and the accessible facts that anchor them.

questions.question: Stevie Wonder performed 'Superstition' on Soul Train during Season 2 — bringing one of the era's biggest hits to the show during its celebrated chart run. 'Superstition' appeared on which Stevie Wonder album?
choices: Songs in the Key of Life

metadata.fact: 'Superstition' was released on October 24, 1972, as the lead single from Talking Book — Stevie Wonder's fifteenth studio album. His Soul Train performance in Season 2 (1972-1973) came during the song's chart run.
metadata.storyHook: One of the greatest albums in soul history. One of the greatest TV performances in Soul Train history. Stevie Wonder brought Talking Book to the stage.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Superstition' was released October 24, 1972, as the lead single from Talking Book. Soul Train Season 2 performance confirmed. CORRECTION: draft stem incorrectly stated performance predated release — sourcing confirms it came AFTER the October 1972 release. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superstition_(song), Apple Music https://music.apple.com/us/album/talking-book/1440808973

sources.title: Talking Book – Apple Music album notes

questions.question: The Jackson 5's Soul Train performance of 'Dancing Machine' in 1973 made pop culture history when a teenage Michael Jackson popularized which robotic dance move on national television?

metadata.fact: Michael Jackson's performance of The Robot during the Jackson 5's Soul Train appearance in 1973 popularized the move on national television — though Jackson did not invent it. The performance became one of the most memorable moments in the show's history.
metadata.storyHook: One television performance. A teenage Michael Jackson. The Robot became a national phenomenon overnight.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Michael Jackson popularized The Robot during the Jackson 5's 1973 Soul Train performance of 'Dancing Machine.' Source: Reddit discussion https://www.reddit.com/r/MichaelJackson/comments/1nan354/michael_jackson_created_the_infamous_robot_dance/

sources.title: Michael Jackson popularized The Robot during Soul Train performance – Reddit discussion

questions.question: Labelle — who performed 'Lady Marmalade' on Soul Train in 1974 — was fronted by which vocalist who became one of R&B's most celebrated solo performers?

metadata.fact: Labelle consisted of Patti LaBelle, Nona Hendryx, and Sarah Dash. Patti LaBelle fronted the group and later launched a celebrated solo career after the group disbanded in 1976.
metadata.storyHook: Three voices. One stage. Patti LaBelle brought 'Lady Marmalade' to Soul Train and left a memory that never faded.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Labelle was fronted by Patti LaBelle. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labelle

questions.question: Soul Train — the groundbreaking R&B variety show that became Black America's essential television stage — was created and hosted by which television personality?

metadata.fact: Don Cornelius created Soul Train, first airing it locally on WCIU-TV in Chicago in August 1970 before taking it to national syndication in October 1971. He hosted the show for over two decades.
metadata.storyHook: Don Cornelius built the stage. Then he invited everyone worth watching to stand on it.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Don Cornelius created and hosted Soul Train. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_Train
metadata.hostNote: Don Cornelius died on February 1, 2012. Do not reference his death or personal circumstances in live delivery unless directly asked.

questions.question: James Brown — who performed 'The Payback' on Soul Train in 1974 — was known by which honorific that captured his singular influence on American music?
choices: The Hardest Working Man in Show Business

metadata.fact: 'The Godfather of Soul' was James Brown's defining title — reflecting his foundational role in the development of funk, R&B, and soul. His 1974 Soul Train performance of 'The Payback' remains one of the show's most electrifying appearances.
metadata.storyHook: The Godfather of Soul on the most important soul stage in America. James Brown and Soul Train were a natural pairing.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: James Brown's title is 'The Godfather of Soul.' Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Brown

questions.question: Al Green's 'Take Me to the River' — performed on Soul Train in 1975 — was later covered by which band, whose 1978 version became a defining record of the new wave era?

metadata.album: More Songs About Buildings and Food
metadata.fact: Talking Heads recorded 'Take Me to the River' for their 1978 album More Songs About Buildings and Food. Their version became a breakout single and introduced the song to rock and new wave audiences.
metadata.storyHook: A Memphis soul record from 1974. A New York art-rock band in 1978. Talking Heads heard something in 'Take Me to the River' that transcended genre — and they were right.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Talking Heads covered 'Take Me to the River' on More Songs About Buildings and Food (1978). Source: Sunny 107.9 https://www.sunny1079.com/talking-heads-release-live-take-me-to-the-river-from-more-songs-about-buildings-and-food-box-set/

sources.title: Talking Heads release live 'Take Me to the River' from 'More Songs About Buildings and Food' – Sunny 107.9

questions.question: Rick James's 'Super Freak' — performed on Soul Train in 1981 — was the basis for which 1990 hip-hop hit that topped the Billboard Hot 100?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 1 OF 3 — RICK JAMES'S MOST SAMPLED SONG'S MOST FAMOUS SAMPLER

metadata.song: Super Freak / U Can't Touch This
metadata.fact: MC Hammer's 'U Can't Touch This' (1990) was built on a sample of Rick James's 'Super Freak,' becoming one of the most commercially successful samples in hip-hop history and topping the Billboard Hot 100.
metadata.storyHook: Rick James performed it on Soul Train in 1981. MC Hammer sampled it in 1990. 'Super Freak' became one of the most recognizable bass lines in American music history.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'U Can't Touch This' sampled 'Super Freak.' Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U_Can%27t_Touch_This

reserve.question: Rufus's 'Tell Me Something Good' — their landmark Soul Train moment in 1974 — was written specifically for the group by which other Soul Train legend?

metadata.fact: 'Tell Me Something Good' was written by Stevie Wonder for Rufus — he tailored the song to Chaka Khan's voice after hearing the group and deciding they needed a track built around her power.
metadata.storyHook: Stevie Wonder heard Rufus. Heard Chaka Khan. Wrote them a song. Then Soul Train made it a national moment.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Tell Me Something Good' was written by Stevie Wonder for Rufus. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tell_Me_Something_Good, Wikipedia Chaka Khan article https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaka_Khan

sources.title: Chaka Khan – early career with Rufus

reserve.question: New Edition's debut 'Candy Girl' — performed on Soul Train in 1983 — was produced by which music executive who later created New Kids on the Block?

metadata.fact: Maurice Starr produced and arranged 'Candy Girl' and shaped New Edition's debut sound. After the group split from him, he applied a similar formula to create New Kids on the Block.
metadata.storyHook: Maurice Starr built New Edition. New Edition outgrew him. He went back to the drawing board and built New Kids on the Block.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Maurice Starr produced 'Candy Girl' and later created New Kids on the Block. Source: Shatter The Standards https://www.shatterthestandards.com/p/the-sweet-sounds-of-new-editions

sources.title: The Sweet Sounds of New Edition's 'Candy Girl' – Shatter The Standards

reserve.question: Soul Train's host Don Cornelius closed every episode with which iconic sign-off phrase — 'Wishing you love, peace, and ___'?

metadata.fact: 'Love, peace, and soul' was Soul Train's famous closing phrase — spoken by Don Cornelius at the end of every episode for over two decades.
metadata.storyHook: Every episode. Same sign-off. 'Love, peace, and soul.' Don Cornelius said it so many times it became part of the American vocabulary.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Love, peace, and soul' was Soul Train's closing catchphrase. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_Train

reserve.question: Zapp & Roger's 'Computer Love' — performed on Soul Train in 1986 — featured Roger Troutman's distinctive vocals created using which electronic voice effects device?

metadata.fact: Roger Troutman's signature talkbox technique — feeding an instrument's signal through a tube into his mouth while singing — became one of the most recognizable sounds in 1980s funk.
metadata.storyHook: Roger Troutman and the talkbox. One of the most distinctive sounds in Soul Train history — and in 1980s R&B.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Roger Troutman used a talkbox on 'Computer Love.' Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Troutman

rounds.name: DEEP CUTS
rounds.description: The music, songwriting, and production behind Soul Train's landmark performances.

questions.question: Marvin Gaye's 'Let's Get It On' — performed on Soul Train in 1974 — was co-written by which lyricist whose spiritual perspective shaped the song's framing of love and sexuality as inseparable?

metadata.fact: Ed Townsend co-wrote 'Let's Get It On' with Marvin Gaye. Townsend originally wrote the song with a religious theme after leaving rehab, emphasizing the unity of physical and spiritual love.
metadata.storyHook: A man fresh out of rehab wrote about love, spirituality, and liberation. Marvin Gaye turned it into a cultural event. Ed Townsend made it possible.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Ed Townsend co-wrote 'Let's Get It On' with Marvin Gaye. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let%27s_Get_It_On_(song)

questions.question: Joe Tex performed 'I Gotcha' on Soul Train in 1972 during the show's first national season. The song was recorded for which independent label associated with Nashville producer Buddy Killen?

metadata.fact: Joe Tex recorded 'I Gotcha' for Dial Records — a Nashville-based independent label associated with producer Buddy Killen. Killen produced Tex's key run of Southern soul recordings.
metadata.storyHook: Nashville. Independent. Buddy Killen behind the board. Joe Tex and Dial Records made the kind of soul that didn't need a major label.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Joe Tex recorded 'I Gotcha' for Dial Records; Buddy Killen is listed as producer. Source: WhoSampled credits https://www.whosampled.com/Joe-Tex/I-Gotcha/

sources.title: I Gotcha by Joe Tex – WhoSampled credits

questions.question: 'Lady Marmalade' — Labelle's soul classic featuring the famous French chorus — was written by which pair of songwriters?

metadata.fact: 'Lady Marmalade' was written by Bob Crewe and Kenny Nolan. The song's Creole-inflected narrative and French chorus were Crewe and Nolan's invention, brought to life by Labelle's extraordinary performance.
metadata.storyHook: Bob Crewe and Kenny Nolan wrote the song. Allen Toussaint produced it in New Orleans. Labelle performed it on Soul Train. 'Lady Marmalade' belongs to all of them.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Lady Marmalade' was written by Bob Crewe and Kenny Nolan. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Marmalade

questions.question: Soul Train first aired locally in Chicago in 1970. In which year did it make its national syndicated debut — beginning its run as the most important Black music television show in America?

metadata.fact: Soul Train debuted in national syndication on October 2, 1971 — after a year of local Chicago airings on WCIU-TV beginning in August 1970.
metadata.storyHook: One year local. Then national. October 2, 1971. Soul Train was everywhere.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Soul Train debuted in national syndication on October 2, 1971. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_Train

questions.question: Rufus's 'Tell Me Something Good' highlighted the powerhouse vocals of which singer — who became the group's defining voice after joining in the early 1970s?

metadata.fact: Chaka Khan joined Rufus in the early 1970s and became the group's signature voice. Her performance on 'Tell Me Something Good' established her as one of the era's most commanding soul singers.
metadata.storyHook: Chaka Khan and Rufus. One of the great band-vocalist pairings in 1970s R&B. 'Tell Me Something Good' was the proof.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Chaka Khan joined Rufus in the early 1970s and sang on 'Tell Me Something Good.' Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaka_Khan, Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tell_Me_Something_Good

questions.question: The Jackson 5's 'Dancing Machine' — the vehicle for Michael Jackson's Robot performance during their 1973 Soul Train appearance — was released on which label?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 2 OF 3 — THE JACKSON 5'S LABEL IN 1973

metadata.fact: The Jackson 5 were signed to Motown Records from 1968 to 1975. 'Dancing Machine' was recorded during their final years on the label.
metadata.storyHook: Motown. 1973. The Jackson 5 still had a year and a half left on the label. They used the time well.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Dancing Machine' was released on Motown Records in 1973. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancing_Machine

reserve.question: Soul Train featured a famous recurring segment where performers formed two parallel lines and each took turns dancing solo down the center. What was this segment called?

metadata.fact: The Soul Train Line — where participants formed two parallel lines and each danced solo down the center — became one of the show's most iconic and widely imitated formats.
metadata.storyHook: Two lines. One aisle. Every dancer's moment. The Soul Train Line was the show inside the show.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: The Soul Train Line was a recurring dance segment on the show. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_Train

reserve.question: Cameo's celebrated performance of 'Word Up!' for Soul Train's platform actually took place at which specific annual event — not a regular episode — in 1987?
choices: Soul Train Lady of Soul Awards

metadata.fact: Cameo performed 'Word Up!' at the 1987 Soul Train Music Awards — a separate annual event from the regular weekly program. The performance is frequently mislabeled online as a standard Soul Train episode.
metadata.storyHook: Not the show. The awards. Cameo performed 'Word Up!' at the Soul Train Music Awards in 1987 — a distinction that matters if you care about the archive.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Cameo performed at the 1987 Soul Train Music Awards, not a regular episode. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_Train_Music_Awards

reserve.question: Al Green's 'Take Me to the River' — performed on Soul Train in 1975 — was co-written by Green alongside which guitarist and Hi Records session musician?

metadata.fact: 'Take Me to the River' was co-written by Al Green and Mabon 'Teenie' Hodges — the Hi Records guitarist whose work on Green's recordings was central to the Memphis soul sound of the era.
metadata.storyHook: Al Green wrote the melody. Teenie Hodges co-wrote the song. Hi Records recorded it. Talking Heads eventually covered it. 'Take Me to the River' traveled far.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Take Me to the River' co-written by Al Green and Mabon 'Teenie' Hodges. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take_Me_to_the_River

sources.title: Take Me to the River – song entry

rounds.name: HIDDEN GEMS
rounds.description: The archival stories behind Soul Train's most celebrated moments — and the history of the show itself.

questions.question: Stevie Wonder originally composed 'Superstition' for which British rock guitarist — whose own version was released on the album Beck, Bogert & Appice in 1973 — before Wonder released his own version on Talking Book?

metadata.fact: Stevie Wonder wrote 'Superstition' for Jeff Beck as part of a collaboration arrangement. Motown pushed Wonder's version out in October 1972 to drive Talking Book sales. Beck's version appeared later on Beck, Bogert & Appice (1973).
metadata.storyHook: Stevie Wonder wrote it for Jeff Beck. Then Motown released Wonder's version first. Then Beck released his. One song, two visions, and one of them became a landmark.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Superstition' was written for Jeff Beck; his version appeared on Beck, Bogert & Appice (not Rough and Ready — CORRECTED from draft). Sources: Apple Music Talking Book notes https://music.apple.com/us/album/talking-book/1440808973, Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superstition_(song)

sources.title: Talking Book – Apple Music album notes

questions.question: Soul Train premiered nationally in 1971 and aired until 2006. Its creator Don Cornelius first launched the local version on WCIU-TV in which American city in August 1970?

metadata.fact: Don Cornelius first aired Soul Train on WCIU-TV in Chicago in August 1970. After a year of local airings, the show went to national syndication on October 2, 1971.
metadata.storyHook: Before the nation. Before the legend. Soul Train was a local Chicago show on WCIU. Don Cornelius built something from nothing.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Soul Train first aired on WCIU-TV in Chicago in August 1970 before national syndication in October 1971. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_Train
metadata.hostNote: Don Cornelius died February 1, 2012. Do not reference his death in live delivery unless directly asked.

questions.question: Soul Train — which premiered nationally in 1971 — aired its final episode in which year, making it the longest-running first-run syndicated music program in American television history?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 3 OF 3 — SOUL TRAIN'S FINAL YEAR

metadata.fact: Soul Train aired its final episode on March 25, 2006 — ending a run from October 2, 1971 that made it the longest-running first-run syndicated music program in American television history.
metadata.storyHook: October 2, 1971. March 25, 2006. 35 years. Soul Train was the longest-running first-run syndicated music program in American TV history.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Soul Train's final episode aired March 25, 2006; confirmed as longest-running first-run syndicated music program. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_Train

reserve.question: Joe Tex — who appeared on Soul Train in 1972 — took his stage name from his home state of Texas. What was his birth name?

metadata.fact: Joe Tex was born Joseph Arrington Jr. — his stage name a tribute to the state of Texas that shaped him.
metadata.storyHook: Joseph Arrington Jr. from Baytown, Texas. He went by Joe Tex. One of the great names in Southern soul history.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Joe Tex was born Joseph Arrington Jr. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Tex

reserve.question: Labelle's 'Lady Marmalade' appeared on which 1974 album — the group's commercial breakthrough — produced by Allen Toussaint at Sea-Saint Recording Studios in New Orleans?

metadata.fact: Nightbirds (1974) was produced by Allen Toussaint at Sea-Saint Recording Studios in New Orleans — the combination of New Orleans production and Labelle's avant-garde soul persona made it one of the era's most distinctive albums.
metadata.storyHook: Allen Toussaint. Sea-Saint Studios. New Orleans. Labelle walked in as an R&B group and walked out with Nightbirds. 'Lady Marmalade' changed everything.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Nightbirds (1974) produced by Allen Toussaint and contained 'Lady Marmalade.' Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nightbirds_(Labelle_album), Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Marmalade
